subject: Follow-up: effective unit cost with prefix cache & next steps
messages:
From: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
To: Alex Chen <alex@finworks.com>, Priya Singh <priya@finworks.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-28T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: caching assumptions, target $/1M tokens, and next steps

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap and a few asks so we can produce a scoped pricing estimate that maps to your budget: 

Summary of what we heard
- Monthly token volume (estimate): 1.2B tokens/month (chat + limited generative workflows)
- Budget range you mentioned: $6k–$12k / month initially (pilot)
- Target effective unit cost: ~ $8 / 1M tokens (you said target was below $10)
- Constraints: must keep PII out of logs; likely VPC/private deployment for pilot later

What we need from you to finalize the estimate
1) Confirm the 1.2B tokens/month is realistic (ballpark OK). Is that average or peak?
2) Confirm target effective $/1M tokens you want us to aim for post-caching. You mentioned sub-$10 — would $8 be a hard constraint or a stretch target?
3) Any hard SLAs/latency SLOs we need to preserve for the pilot?

Caching assumptions we plan to use (proposal)
- Prefix cache for common prompts (30–60% hit rate candidate)
- Cached-token cost model: cached tokens cost ~5–15% of uncached token cost (depends on placement + KV cache hit efficiency)
- Effective unit-cost formula we will show: effective_cost = baseline_cost * (1 - hit_rate) + cached_cost * hit_rate

Example quick calc for baseline calibration (we'll run detailed numbers in the attached spreadsheet):
- Baseline model unit cost (running on dedicated infra, non-cached): $20 / 1M tokens
- If prefix cache hit rate = 50% and cached token cost = $2 / 1M tokens -> effective = 20*(1-0.5) + 2*0.5 = $11 / 1M tokens
- To hit $8 / 1M tokens at baseline $20, you need ~67% cache hit (with cached token cost of $2) or cheaper cached token cost (quant+edge).

Next steps / timeline
- If you confirm volumes + target, we'll deliver a revised estimate (line-item: baseline unit cost, cache hit sensitivity table, expected monthly spend) by Thu (2026-07-30).
- Proposed short follow-up call: Thu 7/30 9:30–10:00 PT to review the sensitivity table (I put a tentative invite).

Attaching: redwood_estimate_v1.pdf (rough numbers) and pricing_model_v2.xlsx (workbook with sensitivity tabs).

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Post-demo: caching assumptions, target $/1M tokens, and next steps

Rafael —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Volume: 1.2B tokens/month is an aggressive consolidation across our product lines — call it a "mid" estimate. Peak daily could be ~80M tokens/day during heavy campaign periods.
2) Target unit cost: our procurement team wants the effective unit cost to be <= $9 / 1M tokens for the pilot. $8 would be ideal but represents significant upside.
3) Latency: for core chat flows 95p latency should be <600ms; for background batch-generation we can accept higher latency.

On cache hit rates — from our telemetry on current templates I think 45–55% is plausible for prefix caching across the chat templates we showed. Some templates have 70% overlap; others are highly dynamic.

Can you show two sensitivity cases in the spreadsheet: conservative (35% hit), expected (50% hit), optimistic (65% hit)? Also include a column that assumes cached token cost = 10% of baseline and one that assumes 5% (to model caching + quantization).

We'll plan to review on Thu 7/30. Priya is the procurement lead; copying her for timelines.

— Alex
Alex Chen
Head of Product, FinWorks
alex@finworks.com

Thanks for the detail. Rafael and I updated the workbook: pricing_model_v2.xlsx now has three sensitivity tabs (conservative/expected/optimistic) with the two cached-token cost assumptions (10% and 5%). Quick highlights from the expected case (50% hit, cached cost = 10% of baseline):

- Baseline unit cost assumed: $22 / 1M tokens (this is representative of the generative model family we demoed on dedicated infra)
- Expected effective cost @ 50% hit: 22*(0.5) + 2.2*(0.5) = $12.1 / 1M tokens
- Optimistic effective cost @ 65% hit (cached cost 5% of baseline): 22*(0.35) + 1.1*(0.65) = $8.085 / 1M tokens

Ben — can you prepare a short note on what dedicated pool sizing would look like for 80M peak and bring a rough monthly infra charge (so we can map line-item infra + platform fee)?

- Expected (50% hit, cached cost = 10%): effective = $12.1 / 1M tokens
- Optimistic (65% hit, cached cost = 5%): effective = $8.1 / 1M tokens

If procurement is comfortable with the expected case (~$12 / 1M tokens) for the pilot, we can propose a 3-month pilot at that effective unit cost with monthly checkpoints (hit-rate telemetry + prompt set analyses) and a clause to rebaseline after month 1. If your requirement is strict <= $9 / 1M tokens we should align on the templates/top-25 list so we can push the hit rate to the optimistic band.

Proposed next steps (post-call):
- FinWorks: share top-25 templates and confirm pilot budget band (by EOD Fri 7/31).
- Redwood: finalize SOW and a pilot pricing addendum reflecting the sensitivity table (draft by Mon 8/3).

See you on the call — Rafael
